[center][b][color=#6aa84f][size=4]A dynamic farm economy overhaul built around market pressure, regional demand, crop rotation, local production, taxation, and long-term diversification.[/size][/color][/b][/center]
Harvest Ledger is an economy and farm-management mod designed to make selling decisions more meaningful without suddenly cutting the value of your products.
Instead of using fixed sales thresholds or scheduled price reductions, the mod creates a continuously changing regional market. Selling large quantities of the same product gradually increases market pressure, while diversification, seasonal subsidies, demand events, crop rotation, and local processing help your farm recover and adapt.
The goal is not to punish profitable farms. The goal is to make long-term specialization something the player actively manages.

[b][color=#f9cb9c][size=3]Core features include:[/size][/color]

[/b]
[list]
[*][b][color=#f9cb9c][size=3]Item-based seasonal market pressure that gradually reduces prices as large quantities are sold.[/size][/color][/b][/*]
[*][b][color=#f9cb9c][size=3]Daily market recovery, improved by selling products from multiple categories.[/size][/color][/b][/*]
[*][b][color=#f9cb9c][size=3]A randomly selected seasonal subsidized crop that can reduce taxes.[/size][/color][/b][/*]
[*][b][color=#f9cb9c][size=3]Temporary regional demand events that increase the value of selected product categories.[/size][/color][/b][/*]
[*][b][color=#f9cb9c][size=3]Crop rotation bonuses based on the previous crop category planted on each tile.[/size][/color][/b][/*]
[*][b][color=#f9cb9c][size=3]Local processing bonuses for artisan goods made from ingredients produced on the farm.[/size][/color][/b][/*]
[*][b][color=#f9cb9c][size=3]A local apiary-quality system based on nearby flower quantity and diversity.[/size][/color][/b][/*]
[*][b][color=#f9cb9c][size=3]Market Exposure warnings and additional pressure for farms that depend too heavily on one income category.[/size][/color][/b][/*]
[*][b][color=#f9cb9c][size=3]Progressive income tax, land-use tax, and configurable automation tax.[/size][/color][/b][/*]
[*][b][color=#f9cb9c][size=3]Optional additional stamina costs for tools and equipment.[/size][/color][/b][/*]
[*][b][color=#f9cb9c][size=3]An in-game Ledger interface showing sales, estimated taxes, market pressure, demand events, subsidy progress, recovery rate, and farm policy information.[/size][/color][/b][/*]
[/list][b][color=#b45f06][size=4]Dynamic Market Pressure[/size][/color][/b]

Every sellable item has its own seasonal market pressure

As more of an item is sold during the season, its pressure gradually rises and reduces its selling price. Different product categories build pressure at different rates, so highly processed or commercially valuable goods may saturate the market faster than basic crops.
The system uses a smooth curve rather than hard sales tiers. There is no single shipment that suddenly cuts an item's value in half.
Market pressure is reset at the end of each season and partially recovers every morning.
[line]
[b][color=#b45f06][size=4]Daily Market Recovery[/size][/color][/b]

Market pressure naturally declines each day.
Recovery becomes stronger when the player sells products from several different categories. Farms that diversify their shipments recover more quickly than farms that repeatedly sell only one type of product.
Meeting the seasonal crop subsidy conditions also grants an additional recovery bonus.
This means market pressure is not permanent. Players can actively respond to it by changing what they produce and sell.
[line]
[b][color=#b45f06][size=4]Seasonal Subsidized Crop[/size][/color][/b]

On the first day of each season, one crop is randomly selected as the subsidized crop.
A farm qualifies for the daily subsidy when:
[list]
[*]At least 25 subsidized crops are currently planted.[/*]
[*]Subsidized crops represent at least 25% of all planted crops.[/*]
[/list]Each qualifying day grants an additional 1% seasonal tax reduction.
The reduction accumulates throughout the season and resets when the next season begins.
[line]
[b][color=#b45f06][size=4]Regional Demand Events[/size][/color][/b]

Each season generates two temporary regional demand events.
Demand events last for seven days and increase the value of selected product categories. Examples include:
[list]
[*]Festival demand for vegetables and flowers.[/*]
[*]Mining supply orders for minerals and monster loot.[/*]
[*]Fish-market shortages.[/*]
[*]Pantry restocking for fruit and animal products.[/*]
[*]Artisan fairs for processed goods.[/*]
[/list]Demand events create temporary opportunities and encourage players to adjust production according to current market conditions.
The active events, affected categories, and remaining duration are shown in the Ledger interface.
[line]
[b][color=#b45f06][size=4]Crop Rotation[/size][/color][/b]

Harvest Ledger records the crop category previously planted on each farm tile.
Planting a different crop category on the same tile in the following season builds a crop-rotation streak and grants a selling bonus:
[list]
[*]One successful rotation: +3%[/*]
[*]Two consecutive rotations: +5%[/*]
[*]Three or more consecutive rotations: +7%[/*]
[/list]Planting the same crop category again resets the rotation streak.
Crop rotation is tracked by category rather than by individual crop, including roots, vines, grains, flowers, leafy vegetables, and fruiting vegetables.
[line]
[b][color=#b45f06][size=4]Local Processing Trace[/size][/color][/b]

Artisan products can receive a local-processing bonus when their ingredients were produced on the player's farm during the current season.
The maximum bonus is 5%, but it is reduced by the market pressure of the original ingredient.
For example, locally produced wheat may improve the value of beer, but heavily saturated wheat cannot be completely protected simply by processing it.
This allows artisan production to soften market pressure without becoming a complete economic bypass.
[line]
[b][color=#b45f06][size=4]Apiary Quality[/size][/color][/b]

Bee Houses use a local pollination-quality system.
Each Bee House checks flowers within five tiles. Honey quality is determined by:
[list]
[*]The number of nearby flowers.[/*]
[*]The number of different flower types nearby.[/*]
[/list]Six flowers and three flower varieties are enough to reach maximum pollination quality.
Higher apiary quality increases the flower contribution to honey value, rewarding carefully designed flower fields and diverse apiary layouts instead of large, uniform Bee House grids.
[line]
[b][color=#b45f06][size=4]Market Exposure[/size][/color][/b]

Market Exposure is a long-term risk system for farms that rely too heavily on one income category.
Every day, the mod checks how much of the farm's income came from its highest-earning category.
Exposure develops gradually through four states:
[list]
[*]Stable[/*]
[*]Watch[/*]
[*]Exposed[/*]
[*]Concentrated[/*]
[/list]Stable and Watch have no direct price penalty. They primarily provide information and early warnings.
At higher states, the dominant category generates additional market pressure. This makes prolonged dependence on a single industry less sustainable without punishing short-term specialization.
Exposure can be reduced by diversifying income. It can also be cleared after several days of maintaining a more balanced sales structure.
A temporary transition-protection period is granted when the farm makes meaningful progress toward diversification.
[line]
[b][color=#b45f06][size=4]Tax System[/size][/color][/b]

Harvest Ledger includes four connected tax components:
Income Tax
Seasonal income is taxed through progressive brackets, ranging from 6% to 16%.
Land-Use Tax
Used farmland beyond the initial tax-free allowance creates an additional land-use cost.
Automation Tax
Profit-generating machines such as Kegs, Preserves Jars, Crystalariums, Casks, Bee Houses, Fish Smokers, and Dehydrators contribute to automation tax.
Automation tax uses a square-root formula, so large machine networks cost more to operate without creating an excessively harsh linear penalty.
Subsidy Reduction
The seasonal crop subsidy reduces the final tax bill based on the number of qualifying days accumulated during the season.
[line]
Optional Stamina Balancing
The mod can apply configurable additional stamina costs to:
[list]
[*]Hoe[/*]
[*]Watering Can[/*]
[*]Pickaxe[/*]
[*]Axe[/*]
[*]Fishing Rod[/*]
[*]Scythe[/*]
[*]Weapons[/*]
[/list]Tool costs may scale with upgrade level, while other equipment can use flat configurable values.
Scythes and weapons have no additional stamina cost by default.

[line]
[center][color=#bf9000][size=6][b][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/images/1303/84247033-1784022565.png[/img][/b][/size][/color][/center]
[left][color=#f9cb9c]Harvest Ledger supports multiplayer farms with host-authoritative end-of-day settlement to ensure consistent economic calculations for all players.
When using Separate Wallets, each player’s shipping income is tracked independently. Taxes are calculated and deducted separately based on each player’s own earnings, and any unpaid taxes remain recorded in that player’s personal ledger.
Shared farm expenses are distributed among players based on their share of shipping income over the previous 7 days by default. This behavior can be changed in [b]config.json:[/b][/color]

[list]
[*][color=#f9cb9c]IncomeShare — Shared expenses are distributed proportionally based on each player’s recent shipping income.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#f9cb9c]Equal — Shared expenses are divided equally among all players.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#f9cb9c]HostPays — The host pays all shared expenses.[/color][/*]
[/list][color=#f9cb9c]The Ledger Interface prioritizes each player’s personal taxes, income, and transaction details. An optional farm-wide tax overview is also available and can be disabled through the ShowFarmTaxOverview [/color][color=#f9cb9c]configuration option.
When using Shared Wallets, Harvest Ledger treats the farm economy as a single financial unit and performs settlement accordingly.[/color][/left]
[center][/center]

[size=6]Recommended Default Settings[/size]
The default configuration is designed to provide noticeable economic management without making normal progression excessively restrictive.
Most systems can be adjusted through the configuration file, including:
[list]
[*]Market saturation speed[/*]
[*]Maximum market penalty[/*]
[*]Minimum and maximum price multipliers[/*]
[*]Daily recovery rates[/*]
[*]Crop-rotation bonuses[/*]
[*]Processing-trace bonus[/*]
[*]Apiary radius and flower targets[/*]
[*]Exposure thresholds[/*]
[*]Tax rates[/*]
[*]Automation tax rate[/*]
[*]Additional stamina costs[/*]
[/list][line]
[center][b][color=#e69138][size=6][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/images/1303/84247033-1784022690.png[/img][/size][/color][/b][/center]
[center][/center]
Harvest Ledger is designed as a configurable economy overhaul.
Mods that directly replace selling prices, taxation systems, machine economics, honey pricing, or crop metadata may require compatibility patches or configuration adjustments.
For the best experience, avoid running multiple full economy-overhaul mods at the same time unless explicit compatibility is confirmed.

[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/images/1303/84247033-1784022726.png[/img][/center]
[color=#D4D4D8]1. Install the latest compatible version of SMAPI.

2. Download Harvest Ledger and extract the archive.

3. Place the entire `HarvestLedger` folder into:

`Stardew Valley/Mods`

4. Launch the game through SMAPI.

5. After the first launch, a configuration file will be generated inside the mod folder. You can edit this file to adjust market pressure, recovery rates, taxes, subsidies, stamina costs, and other balance settings.

6. Do not install Harvest Ledger inside another mod folder. The final folder structure should look similar to:

`Stardew Valley/Mods/HarvestLedger/manifest.json`

When updating the mod, replace the old mod files with the new version. Keep a backup of your configuration file if you have changed any settings.

It is recommended to back up your save before installing or updating any major economy overhaul.[/color]
